name: Utamaro
bio: Kitagawa Utamaro  was a Japanese artist. He is one of the most highly regarded designers of ukiyo-e woodblock prints and paintings, and is best known for his bijin ōkubi-e "large-headed pictures of beautiful women" of the 1790s. He also produced nature studies, particularly illustrated books of insects.

paintings.title: Tsuitate no Danjo
paintings.story: Tsuitate no Danjo is a title given to a multicolour print by the Japanese ukiyo-e artist Kitagawa Utamaro. It depicts a young man and woman by a tsuitate partitioning screen. The print delivers the feeling of several layers of translucency as the woman peers through the folded cloth of the man's haori and the man is seen through a silk gauze–covered portion of the tsuitate.
facts: Ukiyo-e art flourished in Japan during the Edo period from the 17th to 19th centuries, and took as its primary subjects courtesans, kabuki actors, and others associated with the "floating world" lifestyle of the pleasure districts.
Alongside paintings, mass-produced woodblock prints were a major form of the genre.

paintings.title: Three Beauties of the Present Day
paintings.story: Three Beauties of the Present Day  is a nishiki-e colour woodblock print from c. 1792–93 by Japanese ukiyo-e artist Kitagawa Utamaro. The triangular composition depicts the profiles of three celebrity beauties of the time: geisha Tomimoto Toyohina, and teahouse waitresses Naniwaya Kita and Takashima Hisa. The print is also known under the titles Three Beauties of the Kansei Era  and Three Famous Beauties .
facts: Their popularity restored Tsutaya's fortunes and made Utamaro's in the 1790s.
Tsutaya's publisher's seal is printed on the left above Hisa's head, and a round censor's seal appears above it.
Later printings lack the title, the names of the beauties, or both, and the position of the publisher's and censor's seals varies slightly.

paintings.title: On Top and Beneath Ryōgoku Bridge
paintings.story: On Top and Beneath Ryōgoku Bridge is a picture made up of six prints designed by the Japanese ukiyo-e artist Utamaro and published in c. 1795–96. The scene depicts numerous people—mainly elegantly dressed women of various social classes—on outings at Ryōgoku Bridge over the Sumida River in Edo. At about 75 by 60 centimetres, the assembled set is the earliest known ukiyo-e picture of such an extravagant size.
facts: Ryōgoku Bridge was the largest bridge over the river in this heavily populated and thriving urban centre.
Nine elegantly-dressed tall women stand or lean on the bridge, watching the river flow beneath.

paintings.story: Musashino is a triptych print by the Japanese ukiyo-e artist Kitagawa Utamaro. It is a mitate-e parody picture that alludes to the story in the 12th section of The Tales of Ise.

paintings.title: Utamakura print No. 01
paintings.story: "Aquatic monsters and a diver woman." (Kappa to Ama). A page from the erotic shunga book Utamakura. In this illustration from 1788, a female diver (ama) is seen sitting on a rock, watching her partner have sex with two aquatic monsters (kappa). To accentuate the erotic charge, the author placed a basket full of bivalves next to the diver, which during the period in which he created the image were associated with female genitalia.
